clue.text: Some might say such a dessert is rather heavy.

definitions.text: Some might say such a dessert is rather heavy.

parts.note: points to a cake named after a unit of weight
the joke: a cake whose very name is a weight must be a heavy one

explanation.surface: A diner grumbles that the pudding sits like a brick.
explanation.walkthrough: The cake was named for its old recipe, a pound each of flour, butter, sugar and eggs, so 'some might say' it is weighty by name.
explanation.definitionFit: This dense cake is a classic American dessert whose name is also a unit of weight.

clue.text: A sign of soft music that could be played on it.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Italian score marking telling players to play quietly

definitions.text: that could be played on it
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the keyboard instrument such music is played on

explanation.walkthrough: One word serves as both the dynamic marking (written p) and the instrument whose full name means soft-loud.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian marking for quiet playing is also the everyday name for the keyboard instrument.

clue.text: An organization that brings up what you do at night shows what one does first with lots of fruit.

definitions.text: what one does first with lots of fruit

parts.note: the UN, the United Nations, is the organization

indicators.note: in a down clue, bringing something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: at night you sleep

explanation.surface: An outfit that rouses sleepers is somehow tied to preparing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a verb phrase: oranges, bananas and the like have their skins removed before eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Many fruits must have their skin stripped off before they can be eaten, the first step in preparing them.

clue.text: Took a chance with bad things, being people used to risks.

parts.note: to dare is to take a risk, so took a chance is the past tense
evils are bad things

explanation.surface: Gamblers who flirted with wickedness are said to be accustomed to danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckless people who habitually court danger for thrills are described by this hyphenated noun.

clue.text: Using a common article, ran up to steal something in the wrong way in Michigan.

definitions.note: the clue names the answer only by where it is: a city in Michigan

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word is set down back to front, the wrong way round

parts.note: to rob is to steal

explanation.surface: Someone with a stolen article is caught running off in a Michigan town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ann Arbor is a city in Michigan, home of the state's main university; the definition is just its location.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is a university town in southeastern Michigan, west of Detroit.

clue.text: Possibly a net result, having stolen jewelry to drag you in.

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of net may be arranged some other way
result here means what comes out when net is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ice is underworld slang for diamonds, especially stolen ones

explanation.surface: A trawl hauls up a jewel thief's loot and lures victims in.
explanation.walkthrough: Ice for diamonds is crime slang, which is why the clue says stolen jewelry.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure or tempt someone into something is to draw them in with an attractive bait.

clue.text: See 11
A raised desk in an early Christian church, with the Lamb out to be shown.

definitions.text: A raised desk in an early Christian church

indicators.note: the word is there to be shown inside the clue's own letters, spanning the two words

parts.note: the answer sits inside these two words, after the first letter

explanation.surface: A church lectern is described, with the Lamb of God motif taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Lamb' suggests Christ in a church setting, but it only contributes letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the elevated reading stand or pulpit from which scripture was read in early churches.

clue.text: Brought up right in the pecan, for instance, just to eat a little bit, as the guest arrives.

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the turned word
in a down clue, brought up means the word reads from the bottom

parts.note: a pecan is an example of a nut
to sup is to take a little food or drink

explanation.surface: A host nibbles nuts as a dinner guest appears at the door.
explanation.definitionFit: When a guest appears or shows up, that person is said to make an appearance, a phrasal verb for arriving.

clue.text: Refusing to go along with things is surrounded by what the non-doer is doing.

definitions.text: Refusing to go along with things

indicators.note: the word is sits inside the longer word that follows

parts.note: someone who does nothing is taking it easy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A refusal to cooperate is pinned on an idle shirker.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing or withstanding pressure to comply is the present participle sense of standing against something.

clue.text: Not quite 20, if it makes you feel any better!

definitions.text: if it makes you feel any better

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls one letter short, losing its last

parts.note: the answer to 20 across, a word for hoping

explanation.surface: Someone offers a cure that nearly works, if only to cheer you up.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference makes this a pair: 20 across is this answer plus one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This common painkiller is taken to relieve pain, so it is what you take to feel better.

clue.text: They were worn once, back at a showing of old poets.

indicators.note: back means the little word at is read the other way round

parts.note: taken as written
bards were the poets and minstrels of old

explanation.surface: Costumes once worn turn up at a show about ancient poets.
explanation.definitionFit: These short sleeveless tunics, worn by medieval heralds and knights, are garments of a past age.

clue.text: In succession you see the pursuer and the pursued.

definitions.text: In succession you see the pursuer and the pursued.

parts.note: the plain meaning: things following in a line
the picture: a hunted creature runs and its hunter chases close behind

explanation.surface: A chase scene is watched as the hunted and the hunter flash past in turn.
explanation.walkthrough: In a chase the pursued is one, and the pursuer comes behind it, so the phrase for successive things describes the chase too.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means consecutively, each following the previous in sequence.

clue.text: Bad credit can be this, as one might point out.

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of credit are spoiled into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lender remarks on how bad credit can turn out.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone the way, or indicate where to go, is to guide or point them there.

clue.text: The Egyptian goddess who exists twice?

wordplay.note: exists is is, and twice says to write it two times

explanation.surface: A question asks which Egyptian deity has a double existence.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the chief mother goddess of ancient Egyptian religion, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Is there a point to wild mice and crazy loons being things that bring your thoughts to a temporary stopping place?

definitions.text: things that bring your thoughts to a temporary stopping place

parts.note: S, south, is one of the compass points

indicators.note: wild says the letters of mice run about in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of loons are scrambled too

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether there is any sense in wild mice and loony birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is there a point' sounds like asking whether it makes sense; the point is the compass point south. It also nods at the mark itself, a dot above a comma.
explanation.definitionFit: These punctuation marks give a pause stronger than a comma but weaker than a full stop.

clue.text: If you like to fiddle around with only large things, this could be your choice.

definitions.text: If you like to fiddle around with only large things, this could be your choice.

parts.note: fiddle reads as fidget, but means a stringed instrument
the picture: an instrument from the big, low end of the family

explanation.surface: Advice for a fidget who only likes handling big objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle around' suggests idle tinkering; it is the stringed-instrument sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest, lowest-pitched member of the old viol family, a big instrument for a string player.

clue.text: The infant needs a thousand commonly just to make a 1 down.

definitions.note: the answer to 1 down is a keyboard instrument; this is one kind of it

parts.note: an infant is a baby
a grand is common slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A baby needs a thousand dollars to become a keyboard instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This smaller horizontal keyboard instrument is a common type for homes and lounges.

clue.text: In place of the oracle, I'd help make it.

indicators.note: make it says the letters of I'd help are worked into the answer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone offers to stand in for a prophet and help build the shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek site where Apollo's priestess gave prophecies was the most famous oracle.

clue.text: Take little notice when it's in a way to get free high-jinks!

indicators.note: it's in says the short word goes inside the longer one

parts.note: an escape is a way of getting free
an ad is a small advertisement or notice

explanation.surface: Pranksters ignore warnings and run riot after breaking loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, reckless adventure or prank is a madcap exploit, the sense of high spirits running free.

clue.text: On the shoe or belt–or in the dish–you hope things don't give way so!

definitions.text: On the shoe or belt–or in the dish
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the metal clasp on a shoe or belt, and the fruit cake baked in a dish

definitions.text: you hope things don't give way so
definitions.meaning: second meaning: as a verb, to collapse under pressure

explanation.walkthrough: A blueberry version is an American coffee cake baked in a dish, so the noun covers the dessert as well as the fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a fastening clasp or a crumb-topped cake, and the verb means to bend and collapse.

clue.text: What a deb does is to form a small company with me, being finally not safe.

parts.note: co is the short form of company
taken as written
in baseball a runner is either safe or out

explanation.surface: A debutante teams up in a tiny firm, and ends up in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: In baseball the umpire calls a runner safe or out, so not safe is the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutante makes her formal entrance into society at a ball, the traditional social launch.

clue.text: Hoping to make a little more than 9?

indicators.note: more than says something is added after the answer to 9

parts.note: the answer to 9 across, a common painkiller
g, a gram, is a little weight

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for a slightly bigger dose than the one prescribed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference pairs this with 9 across, which is this answer less its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ambitious and striving toward a goal is eager and expectant, in the adjective sense of hopeful.

clue.text: A forged dime is about placed where it could be ascribed to a person.

indicators.note: the rearranged coin word goes about, surrounding, the word for placed
a forged coin is a fake one, so the letters of dime are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A counterfeit coin is planted where it can be blamed on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To attribute a fault or quality to someone is to charge or credit it to that person.

clue.text: The letters sure do make something get turned bad.

indicators.note: make says the letters of sure do are used to form a new word

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Letters surely do cause something to go off.
explanation.definitionFit: Milk that has gone off has curdled and acquired a sharp taste, which is what spoiled means.

clue.text: Ready to tackle anything in play?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: willing and up for any challenge
second meaning: a match or sport

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sportsman, but the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both willing or plucky as an adjective and a contest or sport as a noun.

clue.text: An atom to smash, and you can make soup out of it.

definitions.text: you can make soup out of it

indicators.note: smash means the letters of atom to are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physicist splits an atom and ends up making soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A red fruit used as a vegetable is the base of a classic soup.

clue.text: A sweet one may be in the garden, but an ape et it up!

definitions.text: A sweet one may be in the garden

indicators.note: a jokey spelling of ate it up: the letters of ape are chewed into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A monkey raids the garden and eats the flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: A sweet pea is a fragrant climbing garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet variety is a scented climbing plant grown in flower beds, a relative of the vegetable.

clue.text: Most people don't do this–they put two and two together by going down the column. (Sensible things have to!)

definitions.text: Most people don't do this–they put two and two together by going down the column. (Sensible things have to!)

parts.words: put two and two together by going down the column
parts.note: the arithmetic picture: totalling figures in a column
the idiom: what makes sense is said to compute

explanation.surface: A grumble that people no longer total figures by hand down a column.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrasal verb means both to total numbers and to make sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to total a column of numbers, and figuratively to be consistent or logical.

clue.text: Take things off in the outhouse?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to cast off, as a tree drops leaves
second meaning: a small hut in the garden

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests undressing in a privy; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cast off, and the noun is a simple garden hut or outbuilding.

clue.text: See 11
A measure might be, but you have to choose to get sort of dead around it.

indicators.note: around it says the rearranged letters go round the word for choose
sort of suggests a loose reshaping of the letters of dead

parts.note: taken as written
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: A bill might pass, but only if you pick a half-dead version of it.
explanation.walkthrough: A measure here is a bill or motion, which may be passed by a vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion or bill that a legislature formally approves and accepts has been passed into force.

clue.text: Went overboard for this, just to act with little Theodore.

parts.note: to do is to act
Ted is the short, pet form of Theodore

explanation.surface: Someone got carried away over a performance with little Teddy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be excessively fond of someone, lavishing affection on them, is to go too far in love.

clue.text: Ready for the Easter parade?

parts.note: read as prepared, it means wearing one's best clothes
the New York tradition of strolling Fifth Avenue in finery and bonnets

explanation.surface: Are you set for the Easter parade?
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing smart or formal clothes for an occasion is to be in one's finery.
